text: The decision records that Air Canada's support chatbot told a passenger they could request a reduced bereavement fare retroactively within 90 days of ticket issuance. The linked Bereavement travel page said the policy did not apply after travel was completed. The tribunal found Air Canada responsible for information on its website and liable for negligent misrepresentation; the decision does not establish the chatbot's technical architecture.

ai_system_name: Air Canada support chatbot (technical nature not established in the decision)
mitigation_gap: The tribunal found that Air Canada did not take reasonable care to ensure its chatbot was accurate. The decision does not identify the model architecture, technical guardrails, or escalation controls.
reliance_or_harm: The tribunal accepted that the passenger reasonably relied on the chatbot information, purchased two flights, and suffered C$650.88 in damages.
source_review_unresolved: Human decision pending on whether a chatbot whose technical nature was not provided satisfies the corpus AI-attribution rule.
